editorial.brief: Two Marvel promos did the day's heaviest lifting: Spider-Man: Brand New Day topped Wikipedia and trended on YouTube, while a Marvel Rivals character trailer pulled 1.3 million YouTube views and cross-listed on Steam. Everything else — an AI chip deal, a 6.3 quake off the Philippines, a Michigan primary market already settled at 100 percent — ran in parallel without touching it.
editorial.cover_sub: 638,274 reads and a matching YouTube trend put the film two clear laps ahead of anything else Wikipedia logged today.
editorial.wiki_deck: Spider-Man: Brand New Day out-read The Odyssey by two to one, with YouTube trending the same title the same day.
editorial.letter_headline: A superhero sequel, mostly alone at the top
editorial.discourse_deck: Hacker News is quietly technical, debating MCP and Pi over front-page arguments; Lemmy wants sofa-moving advice and a decade-old grudge about a tan suit; Bluesky is commemorative and gentle; Mastodon is arguing about AI policy and Reddit's trustworthiness.
editorial.foreign_deck: The wire ran on AI investment — a Samsung-Broadcom chip pact past $200 billion, Singapore factory output — while search stayed local: a footballer, a festival, an eclipse.
editorial.markets_deck: Today's top markets ranged from settled to speculative: a Michigan primary already at 100 percent, a Dota 2 series near a coin flip, and long-shot geopolitical bets on Hormuz, Iran and Ethiopia all sitting in single digits.
editorial.watch_deck: Counter-Strike 2 held the largest crowd at 1.28 million peak players, with Caedrel drawing 25,479 live viewers as PUBG and Dota 2 both cleared 600,000 players apiece.
editorial.yt_note: The Marvel Rivals trailer led with 1.3 million views, edging out a Violent Night sequel trailer and an Ozuna single, with a burger-restaurant video the one non-franchise entry in the top five.
editorial.closing_note: The Spider-Man numbers, the Marvel Rivals trailer, tonight's Counter-Strike peak — all of it resets by morning. Only the 6.3 quake off Sarangani and whatever the Michigan primary actually decides will still matter once this snapshot is a day old.
wiki_paras: Spider-Man: Brand New Day led Wikipedia with 638,274 views, roughly double the runner-up, The Odyssey (2026 film), on 315,568. Glen Hansard, Zendaya and Tom Holland filled out the top five, the latter two both attached to the same franchise.

The film also trended on YouTube today, which is as close to a paper trail as this data offers. No single review, release date or controversy shows up in the wire or trends feeds to explain the specific timing — just two platforms agreeing on the same title at once.

Two Tom Holland-adjacent names in one top five suggests a fandom mobilizing rather than a news event breaking. On a day with no dominant headline elsewhere, a comic-book sequel becoming the thing everyone looked up is itself the finding.
letter_paras: Today's snapshot has one clear anchor and not much else. Spider-Man: Brand New Day led Wikipedia by two to one and reappeared on YouTube's trending list — the only story to cross feeds twice over. A Marvel Rivals trailer did the same trick between Steam and YouTube, pulling 1.3 million views. Past those two, the day scattered: a chip deal, a quake, a primary market already resolved.

The unglamorous corners were busy in their own way. Lemmy's top post today was how to move a sofa, sitting above a swipe at a president's tan suit from over a decade ago. USGS logged 25 quakes above magnitude 2.5, the largest a 6.3 off the Philippines that never made it near a headline elsewhere. Cloudflare's most-requested domains were, as ever, the plumbing — Google, Apple, Cloudflare itself.

A same-hour snapshot earns its keep on days exactly like this one, when nothing forces itself onto every feed at once. It shows what genuinely traveled across platforms, Spider-Man and a Marvel trailer, against what merely sat atop one, whether that's a sofa-moving thread or a primary market nobody's still betting against. Tomorrow's data will owe nothing to today's.
